statement:
We have not established whether every total category is exact. Equivalently,
we have not proved that every finite parallel family
$a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ has an integral affine post-equalizer.
notes: No proof or counterexample; three ordinary arrows are the least unresolved family size. Stable label: A:main

statement:
For every small category $A$, including the empty category and categories
with several components, the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ is exact;
\item $\colim_A:(\Q\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to\Q\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$
is exact and, for every prime $p$, the functor
$\colim_A:(\F_p\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})^A\to\F_p\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}
No totality hypothesis is needed. Consequently, Parts A.1 and A.2 taken
together ask equivalent universal questions. A negative answer to A.1
necessarily gives a failure over $\Q$ or over at least one prime field,
although the obstructing diagram need not remain the same after reduction.
notes: All small categories; no totality assumption. Reduction, not a decision of the main question. Stable label: A:fieldwise

statement:
We have not established rational exactness for every total category, nor
exactness over each $\F_p$. Proposition~\ref{A:fieldwise} is a reduction,
not a decision of either implication.
notes: Open in this incomplete record: Part A.2 Stable label: A:coefficients

statement:
For a small category $A$, let $\mathcal R_A$ be the smallest class of
covariant integral modules containing every $\mathbb Z[H]$, for
$H:A\to\mathrm{Set}$, and closed under extensions, kernels of
epimorphisms between members, arbitrary direct sums, direct summands,
filtered colimits, and $F\mapsto F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[H]$.
Every member of $\mathcal R_A$ is objectwise torsion-free.
There is a finite filtered category $A$ and three parallel arrows
$a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$ for which
\[
 Q_a=\operatorname{coker}\bigl(P_q\longrightarrow P_p^2,
 \ t\longmapsto(t(a_1-a_0),t(a_2-a_0))\bigr)
 \notin\mathcal R_A.
\]
Thus the first proposed target of approach P1 cannot work uniformly,
even for filtered categories. This does not refute P1's alternative
of finding a different module with the same $T_1$, and it is not a
separator between totality and exactness.
notes: Four objects and seventeen arrows with a terminal object. Q_a(x)=Z^2 plus Z/3. Alternative modules with the same T1 are not excluded. Stable label: A:P1-torsion

statement:
There is a small filtered category $A$ and a triple
$a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$ such that its rational column module
\[
 Q_a=\operatorname{coker}\bigl(
 \mathbb Q[A(q,-)]\longrightarrow\mathbb Q[A(p,-)]^2,\quad
 t\longmapsto(t(a_1-a_0),t(a_2-a_0))\bigr)
\]
does not belong to the smallest class of rational diagrams containing
all permutation modules and closed under extensions, kernels of
epimorphisms, arbitrary direct sums, direct summands, filtered colimits,
and tensoring with permutation modules. This strengthens the integral
torsion obstruction: all values of this example are rational vector
spaces. It does not refute the alternative in P1 of using another
module with the same $T_1$. Moreover, the same category and triple
give an integral column module with torsion-free values which lies
outside the original integral resolving class.
notes: Four-object category with terminal object and one infinite-cyclic automorphism group. Rational obstruction and integral torsion-free strengthening; the even-power invariant includes tensor-permutation closure. Not a separator. Stable label: B:P1-rational

statement:
Let $A$ be a small category with finite hom-sets. Suppose that any two
objects have a common successor. Suppose also that $A$ has the following
morphism Ramsey property: for any objects $p,q$ and positive integer $c$
there is an object $r$ such that every coloring
\[
 \chi:A(p,r)\longrightarrow\{1,\ldots,c\}
\]
admits $g:q\to r$ for which $\chi$ is constant on
$g\circ A(p,q)$. Then $A$ has exact colimits in abelian groups.
More precisely, if $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ and $k\geq1$, every target
$r$ with the stated Ramsey property for $p,q,c=(3k+1)^k$ admits an
integral affine combination $t\in\mathbb Z[A(q,r)]$ satisfying
$ta_0=\cdots=ta_k$.
notes: Proved: a Ramsey criterion for integral exactness Stable label: OG:Ramsey-exact

statement:
It is used above only to give an elementary Smith normal form proof
of extension to the circle. Divisibility makes $\mathbb T$ an injective
abelian group, so the same argument works without finite hom-sets if
one invokes that standard injectivity theorem. The finite version
already covers the ordered-graph application below.
notes: Proved: scope of the finite-hom-set hypothesis Stable label: OG:finite-hom-scope

statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ have one representative of each finite linearly
ordered simple graph as objects and increasing induced graph
embeddings as arrows, composed as functions. Then $\mathcal G$ has
exact colimits in abelian groups. In particular it is not a
counterexample to totality implying exactness.
notes: Proved: ordered finite graphs are exact Stable label: OG:exact

statement:
For the three embeddings $v_0,v_1,v_2$ of the one-vertex graph into
$q$, an integral affine equalizer exists in the ordered graph $r_6$
on $\{0<\cdots<5\}$ with edge set
\[
 \{01,12,13,15,23,24,34,35\}.
\]
It is
\[
 t=(012)-(015)+(124)-(134)+(235).
\]
notes: Proved: three vertex maps Stable label: OG:vertex-certificate

statement:
For the embeddings $e_0,e_1$ of the ordered edge into the two edges
of $q$, an integral affine equalizer exists in the ordered graph $r_7$
on $\{0<\cdots<6\}$ with edge set
\[
 \{01,12,23,35,56,14,45\}.
\]
It is
\[
 t=(012)+(123)+(235)+(356)-(014)-(145)-(456).
\]
notes: Proved: two edge maps Stable label: OG:edge-certificate

statement:
Let $C$ be a skeleton of the category of nonempty finite sets with
an independent linear order and cyclic order, whose arrows are
injections preserving both orders. Cyclic orders on one or two
points are taken to be unique. This small category is neither total
nor exact. More precisely, $BC$ is simply connected and
$H_2(BC;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, and there is a five-arrow parallel
family with no affine equalizer over any nonzero commutative ring.
No assertion that $C$ is quasi-filtered is made.
notes: Refuted: the linear--cyclic order candidate Stable label: A:cyclic-linear

statement:
A small category $A$ has the finite-pattern morphism Ramsey property if,
for every $p,q\in A$, finite subset $S\subset A(p,q)$, and positive
integer $c$, there is $r\in A$ such that every coloring
\[
 \chi:A(p,r)\longrightarrow\{1,\ldots,c\}
\]
admits $g:q\to r$ for which $\chi$ is constant on $gS$.
When all hom-sets are finite, this is equivalent to the morphism Ramsey
property in Theorem~\ref{OG:Ramsey-exact}: take $S=A(p,q)$.
notes: Proved: agreement of the two Ramsey formulations for finite hom-sets Stable label: CD:FPR

statement:
Let $A$ be a small nonempty category with common successors. The following
are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every contravariant diagram $X:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to
\mathrm{CompHaus}$ of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces has a nonempty
strict inverse limit.
\item $A$ has the finite-pattern morphism Ramsey property.
\end{enumerate}
No bound on the hom-sets is assumed.
notes: Proved: compact inverse limits and finite-pattern Ramsey Stable label: CD:compact-Ramsey

statement:
A nonempty small category with common successors satisfying either
condition of Theorem~\ref{CD:compact-Ramsey} has exact abelian colimits.
notes: Proved: the compact assertion implies integral exactness Stable label: CD:compact-exact

statement:
Let $A$ be nonempty, connected, and quasi-filtered. Every contravariant
diagram $X:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Set$ of nonempty finite sets with
$|X(a)|\leq N$ for one finite integer $N$ has a nonempty inverse limit.
notes: One uniform finite size bound; unbounded fibres not covered. Stable label: CD:bounded-fibres

statement:
Let $A=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, which is exact and total, and let
$B(n)$ be the free Boolean algebra on the generators
$x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}$, also regarded as its associated Boolean ring
with addition given by symmetric difference. An increasing injection $f:n\to m$ acts by
$x_i\mapsto x_{f(i)}$. These are injective unital Boolean-algebra
homomorphisms: the corresponding restriction maps on the sets of
Boolean valuations are surjective.

In $B(2)$ the elements $x_0,x_1$ have the same class in
$\colim_A^{\Set}UB$, since the two maps $1\to2$ carry the sole
generator to them. Nevertheless, with $c=x_0$, the pairs
$(c,x_0)$ and $(c,x_1)$ lie in different components of
$\El_A(UB\times UB)$. Equality of the two coordinates is preserved
and reflected by every structure map; it holds for the first pair
and fails for the second.

The failure persists for the abelian colimit after pinning $c$.
Consider the component $E$ of $\El_A UB$ containing $(2,x_0)$.
Its objects are exactly the pairs $(n,x_j)$. Indeed renaming
variables sends a Boolean expression to a generator only if that
expression was itself a generator, as can be checked on valuations.
On $E$, evaluation at the valuation which sends $x_j$ to $1$ and all
other generators to $0$ defines a natural homomorphism of additive
groups
\[
 B(n)\longrightarrow\F_2.
\]
For an arrow $f:(n,x_j)\to(m,x_{f(j)})$, the target valuation
restricts to the specified source valuation, proving naturality.
At $(2,x_0)$ this map takes $x_0$ to $1$ and $x_1$ to $0$.
Consequently $x_0$ and $x_1$ remain distinct in the abelian colimit
over $E$.

Thus moving to a category of elements in order to hold a multiplicative
coefficient fixed need not preserve even a set-colimit relation
available before that move. In a proposed Boolean-algebra argument,
one must prove the needed lifted tuple relations; totality alone
cannot be cited for their existence. This example does not rule out
a different homological argument exploiting the full Boolean identity.
notes: An exact total category can lose an original set-colimit relation after passage to a component of elements that fixes a coefficient. Stable label: CD:pinning-counterexample

statement:
We have not proved that totality implies either condition of
Theorem~\ref{CD:compact-Ramsey}. Nor have we proved or refuted that
exactness implies those conditions. Proposition~\ref{CD:bounded-fibres}
only shows that a finite-valued obstruction for a quasi-filtered
category must have unbounded fiber cardinalities. Signed measures
obtained from affine equalizers cannot be replaced by genuine points
without an additional argument.
notes: Open in this incomplete record: the missing compact implication Stable label: CD:unresolved

statement:
Let $K^*$ be any repaired AKR category covered by
Proposition~\ref{C:akr-all-rings}. For every object $X$ and every
finitely supported family of nonnegative real coefficients
$(t_g)_{g:W\to X}$ with $\sum_g t_g=1$, put
\[
 \mu_i(v)=\sum_{g:\,gv_i=v}t_g\quad
 (v\in K^*(V,X),\ i=1,2,3).
\]
Then
\[
 \|\mu_2-\mu_1\|_1+\|\mu_3-\mu_1\|_1\geq1.
\]
In particular the initial triple has no arbitrarily accurate
simultaneous equalizers obtained from probability combinations of
ordinary arrows, even as the target varies.
notes: All admissible repaired AKR categories; probability combinations have total marginal discrepancy at least one. Stable label: CC:positive-gap

statement:
There is a nonempty connected quasi-filtered small category $A$ and
a contravariant diagram of nonempty finite-dimensional compact convex
sets, with continuous affine transition maps, whose strict inverse
limit is empty. One may take $A=K^*$ as above.
notes: Quasi-filtered example only; neither totality nor its failure is asserted. Stable label: CC:convex-counterexample

statement:
We have not proved or refuted the assertion that every three parallel
arrows in every total category admit an integral affine equalizer.
The least undecided family size is three arrows. The equivalences below
are exact obstruction formulas, not vanishing theorems for those
obstructions. In particular, the vanishing of the row obstruction under
totality does not establish the vanishing of the column obstruction.
notes: Open in this incomplete record: Part B.1 Stable label: B:triple-question

statement:
Let $a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ be a finite family of ordinary arrows in
an arbitrary small category, and let $z_i=a_i-a_0$ for $1\leq i\leq k$.
Put
\[
 d:P_q^k\longrightarrow P_p,\qquad
 (t_i)\longmapsto\sum_i t_i z_i,\qquad K=\ker d,
\]
and let $H$ be $A(p,-)$ modulo all relations $ca_i\sim ca_0$.
Then $\mathbb Z[H]=\operatorname{coker}d$ canonically, and
\begin{align*}
 T_1(\mathbb Z[H])&\cong
 \operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{colim}K\xrightarrow{\epsilon^k}\mathbb Z^k),\\
 T_2(\mathbb Z[H])&\cong
 \ker(\operatorname{colim}K\xrightarrow{\epsilon^k}\mathbb Z^k),\\
 T_j(\mathbb Z[H])&\cong T_{j-2}(K)\quad(j\geq3).
\end{align*}
Consequently, for total $A$, $\epsilon^k$ is an isomorphism and $K$
is colimit-acyclic. For $k=1$ the module
$J_i=P_qz_i\subseteq P_p$ is colimit-acyclic and has zero colimit.
notes: Proved: the row calculation used below Stable label: B:row-audit

statement:
Let $A$ be total and $a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$. Put
$K_i=\ker(P_q\xrightarrow{z_i}P_p)$ and $L=K_1\cap K_2$.
Then the surjection in TOTEX B.1 is a canonical isomorphism
\[
 T_1\bigl(P_q/(K_1+K_2)\bigr)\ \cong\
 \mathbb Z/\epsilon(L).
\]
notes: Both derivations checked, including the sign between their explicit maps. Stable label: B:lead1

statement:
Let $A$ satisfy I; neither connectedness nor nonemptiness is required
in this proposition. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\operatorname{colim}_A:\mathrm{Ab}^A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is exact;
\item for every $p,r\in A$ and every $z\in\mathbb Z[A(p,r)]$
with $\operatorname{aug}z=0$, some affine $t:r\to s$ satisfies $tz=0$.
\end{enumerate}
For every small $A$, every such $p,r,z$, and
$L_z=\ker(P_r\xrightarrow{t\mapsto tz}P_p)$, one has canonically
\[
 T_1(P_p/P_rz)\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L_z).
\]
notes: The Tor formula requires augmentation zero; I is required for the criterion, connectedness is not. Stable label: B:lead2

statement:
For every small category $A$, every integer $k\geq0$ and every family
$a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$, put
\[
 d^{\mathrm t}:P_q\longrightarrow P_p^k,
 \quad t\longmapsto(tz_i)_{i=1}^k,
 \qquad Q_a=\operatorname{coker}d^{\mathrm t},
 \quad L=\ker d^{\mathrm t}.
\]
Then canonically
\begin{align*}
 T_1(Q_a)&\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L),\\
 T_2(Q_a)&\cong\ker(\operatorname{colim}L\to\mathbb Z),\\
 T_i(Q_a)&\cong T_{i-2}(L)\qquad(i\geq3).
\end{align*}
If objects in the component of $q$ have common successors, the family
has an affine equalizer if and only if $T_1(Q_a)=0$.
In the covariant-module presentation, $Q_a$ has $k$ generators $x_i$
at $p$ and one relation $\sum_i(a_i-a_0)x_i=0$ at $q$.
notes: No category hypothesis for the formulas; common successors for the equalizer criterion; k=0 included. Stable label: B:lead3

statement:
Suppose $A$ is nonempty and connected and satisfies I and IV. For
$M:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ and $\alpha,\beta\in M(q)$, equality of their
classes in $\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Set}}_A UM$ implies that
an affine $t:q\to s$ satisfies $t\alpha=t\beta$ in $M(s)$.
Moreover $A$ is exact if and only if, for every such $M,q,\alpha,\beta$,
equality in $\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Ab}}_A M$ implies the
same affine equalizability.
notes: Proved: the precise assertions of Lead 4 Stable label: B:lead4

statement:
The comparison map
\[
 \operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Set}}_A UM\longrightarrow
 U\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{Ab}}_A M
\]
is surjective under the common-successor hypothesis: transport the
finite sum representing an abelian colimit element to one object and
add there. The two assertions above precisely locate the remaining
issue in its fibres: set equality is already sufficient, while abelian
equality may identify additional components. This does not identify
exactness with finite-product preservation of the set-colimit functor.
For example, for $A=\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, $p=[0]$, and $M=P_p$,
the elements $2[a]-[b]$ for distinct $a,b:p\to q$ and $[a]$ have the
same abelian-colimit class. Ordinary increasing injections preserve
the number and coefficients of nonzero basis terms, so these two
elements lie in different set-colimit components. Nevertheless $A$
is exact, by the already audited Isbell example. Thus the final phrase
of Lead 4 is valid as motivation for the difference between the two
colimits, and would be false if read as the asserted equivalence with
siftedness or with injectivity of this comparison.
notes: Exactness is not equivalent to siftedness or injectivity of the set-to-abelian comparison. Stable label: B:lead4-scope

statement:
Let $A$ be a nonempty category in which every pair of objects has a
common successor, and let $F:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$. For $\kappa\in F(s)$,
its colimit class is zero if and only if there are an ordinary arrow
$u:s\to y$, finitely many ordinary parallel pairs
$e_j,e'_j:x_j\rightrightarrows y$, and $k_j\in F(x_j)$, such that
\[
 F(u)\kappa=\sum_j\bigl(F(e_j)-F(e'_j)\bigr)k_j\quad\hbox{in }F(y).
\]
In particular Lead 5(ii) holds; its condition I can be weakened to
common successors.
notes: Common successors suffice. Stable label: B:zero-normal-form

statement:
Let $A$ be total and let $a_0,a_1,a_2:p\to q$.
Use $z_i,K_i,K,L$ as in Lemma~\ref{B:row-audit} and
Proposition~\ref{B:lead1}, and put
$K_3=\ker(P_q\xrightarrow{a_2-a_1}P_p)$.
Choose affine pair equalizers $\rho_1\in K_1(s)$,
$\rho_2\in K_2(s)$ and $\rho_3\in K_3(s)$ at a common object $s$.
Then
\[
 \kappa=(\rho_1-\rho_3,\rho_3-\rho_2)\in K(s)
\]
has zero class in $\operatorname{colim}K$.
If an affine $t:s\to r$ kills $\kappa$, then
$t\rho_1=t\rho_2=t\rho_3$ is an affine equalizer of the triple.
Such a $t$ exists whenever the finitely many pairs in a normal form of
Lemma~\ref{B:zero-normal-form} have a common affine equalizer.
In particular, a normal form with at most one summand implies the
existence of such a $t$.
Finally the natural morphism
\[
 \psi:K_1\oplus K_2\oplus K_3\longrightarrow K,
 \qquad(k_1,k_2,k_3)\longmapsto(k_1-k_3,k_2+k_3)
\]
has kernel canonically isomorphic to $L$, and
\[
 T_1(K/\operatorname{im}\psi)\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L).
\]
notes: Proved: Lead 5(i), (iii), and (iv) Stable label: B:lead5

statement:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{B:lead5}, suppose the triple
has no affine equalizer. Its class $[\kappa]$ in
$\operatorname{colim}I$ is the nonzero generator of
$\ker(\operatorname{colim}I\to\operatorname{colim}K)
\cong\mathbb Z/\epsilon(L)$.
It cannot have a normal form in which every $k_j$ belongs to $I(x_j)$,
and it cannot have a normal form whose pairs have a common affine
equalizer. In particular every one-term normal form is impossible.
notes: A bar chain with module coefficients is intended, not nonzero H1 of BA. Stable label: B:mixed-cycle-obstruction

statement:
For the repaired AKR construction and every admissible choice of its
parameters, the requested assertion is
\[
 H_2\!\left(\El_{K^*}
 \bigl(K^*(V,-)/(cv_1\sim cv_2)\bigr);\Z\right)\ne0.
\]
We have not established this universally quantified assertion or its
negation. Theorem~\ref{C:selected-nontotal} proves infinite-stage
survival for a fully specified choice of sufficiently large targets,
and more generally for such choices over any admissible parameter
sequence. It does not cover every admissible target choice. The
computations concern explicitly identified finite substages and do
not extend that quantifier. The all-coefficient obstruction in
Proposition~\ref{C:akr-all-rings} establishes nonexactness independently
of this unresolved totality question.
notes: Universal admissible-choice survival remains unresolved. Selected sufficiently large targets have proved infinite-stage survival. Stable label: C:survival-question

statement:
Let $A$ and $D$ be small categories, let $u:D\to A$ be a functor, and let
\[
 R=\mathop{\rm colim}_{d\in D}A(-,u(d)):A^{\rm op}\longrightarrow\mathrm{Set}.
\]
Assume that every connected component of every comma category $x\downarrow u$
is weakly contractible. Form $A'$ by adjoining one object $Z$, by setting
$A'(x,Z)=R(x)$ for $x\in A$, by allowing no arrows from $Z$ to $A$, and by
setting $A'(Z,Z)=\{1_Z\}$; composition with arrows of $A$ is the presheaf
action of $R$. Let $H':A'\to\mathrm{Set}$ be any covariant functor, and put
$H=H'|_A$.

Define the two-sided category $E(R,H)$ to have objects $(x,r,k)$ with
$x\in A$, $r\in R(x)$ and $k\in H(x)$. An arrow
$(x,r,k)\to(y,s,l)$ is an arrow $b:x\to y$ of $A$ satisfying
$R(b)s=r$ and $H(b)k=l$. Then the functor
\[
 F:\operatorname{El}_D(u^*H)\longrightarrow E(R,H),\qquad
 (d,k)\longmapsto(u(d),[d,1_{u(d)}],k)
\]
which sends an arrow $\delta:d\to d'$ to $u(\delta)$ is a weak equivalence
on nerves. For every $h\in H'(Z)$ the old comma link
\[
 L_h=(\operatorname{El}_A H)\downarrow (Z,h)
\]
is a full union of connected components of $E(R,H)$. If
$e=\dim ND<\infty$, then $H_j(BL_h;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $j>e$ and the
inclusion induces an injection
\[
 H_j(B\operatorname{El}_A H;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow
 H_j(B\operatorname{El}_{A'}H';\mathbb Z)
 \quad(j>e).
\]
The assertion also holds with arbitrary constant coefficients. If $D$ is
empty, $R$ and all links are empty and adjoining $Z$ adds only isolated
objects to the category of elements.
notes: Proved: the link comparison, with its necessary hypothesis Stable label: C:link-comparison

statement:
Consider a cyclic quasi-filter indexing graph with copies of $S$ at its
vertices and copies of $T$ on its edges, the two maps on each edge being
chosen from a parallel pair $f,g:T\rightrightarrows S$. If an arrow
$c:x\to T$ satisfies $fc=gc$, the component of $x\downarrow u$ containing
these lifts has nonzero first integral homology. If $f$ and $g$ are
monomorphisms, this component is precisely a subdivided circle.
Consequently the comma hypothesis in Proposition~\ref{C:link-comparison}
fails. In the repaired first-stage AKR quasi-filter for $v_1,v_2$, the
last and first maps satisfy $\alpha_{4k}v_1=\alpha_0v_1$, so this
obstruction occurs when quasi-filtering $(\alpha_0,\alpha_{4k})$ at the
next stage.
notes: Proved: the equalizing-precomposition obstruction Stable label: C:link-obstruction

statement:
For every admissible choice in the repaired AKR Construction C.1, for
every nonzero unital commutative ring $R$, and for every object $X$ of
$K^*$, the $R$-linear map
\[
 R[K^*(W,X)]\longrightarrow R[K^*(V,X)]^2,\qquad
 t\longmapsto\bigl(t(v_2-v_1),t(v_3-v_1)\bigr)
\]
is injective. In particular, the three initial point maps have no
$R$-affine equalizer. The same injectivity holds for finitely supported
coefficients in an arbitrary abelian group, with the evident meaning
of the two differences.
notes: Every admissible repaired construction, arbitrary abelian-group coefficients. Stable label: C:akr-all-rings

statement:
Let $A'$ be obtained from $A$ by adjoining one new maximal object $Z$
with identity endomorphism only. Suppose a family
$\alpha_i:T_i\to Z$ ($i\in I$, possibly infinite) generates all incoming
arrows: every $b:X\to Z$, $X\in A$, can be written
$\alpha_i c$ with $c:X\to T_i$ in $A$. For any covariant functor
$F':A'\to\mathrm{Ab}$, write $F=F'|_A$ and
$Q=\operatorname{colim}_A F$. Define homomorphisms
\[
 a:\bigoplus_{i\in I}F(T_i)\longrightarrow F'(Z),\quad
 (x_i)\longmapsto\sum_i F'(\alpha_i)x_i,
 \qquad
 b:\bigoplus_{i\in I}F(T_i)\longrightarrow Q,\quad
 (x_i)\longmapsto\sum_i[x_i].
\]
Then, canonically,
\[
 \operatorname{colim}_{A'}F'
 \cong (Q\oplus F'(Z))/\{(b(x),-a(x)):x\in\bigoplus_iF(T_i)\},
\]
\[
 \ker(Q\to\operatorname{colim}_{A'}F')=b(\ker a).
\]
For the AKR action
$H=h_V/(cv_1\sim cv_2)$, put
$K(X)=\ker(\mathbb Z[A(W,X)]\xrightarrow{,v_2-v_1,}
\mathbb Z[A(V,X)])$. Thus $K(X)$ is the integral cycle group of the
graph whose vertices are $V$-arrows and whose edges are $W$-arrows,
with edge $c$ directed from $cv_1$ to $cv_2$. For a quasi-filter
attachment all $T_i=T$. Its old-to-new map on $H_2(B\operatorname{El}H)$
is injective if and only if
\[
 \sum_i\alpha_i\kappa_i=0\ \text{in }K(Z)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \left[\sum_i\kappa_i\right]=0\ \text{in }\operatorname{colim}_A K
\]
for every finitely supported family $\kappa_i\in K(T)$.
notes: Proved: an exact cycle-space test for one attachment Stable label: C:attachment-cycle-test

statement:
The unqualified phrase ``the component is a circle'' in Lead~7 is
false if it is read without the monomorphism hypothesis of the AKR
application. Let $A$ have objects $x,T,S$, arrows
\[
 A(x,T)=\{c,d\},\qquad A(T,S)=\{f,g\},\qquad A(x,S)=\{h\},
\]
identity endomorphisms only, no other arrows, and the four compositions
$fc=fd=gc=gd=h$. Composition with identities is prescribed in the
usual way. This is a complete finite category: there are no three
composable nonidentity arrows, and the identity laws settle every
remaining associativity equation.

Take the five-vertex cyclic quasi-filter indexing graph ($k=1$).
It has copies $S_i$ of $S$ and copies $T_i$ of $T$, with two arrows
from $T_i$ to $S_i,S_{i+1}$ (cyclic indices), mapped by $u$ to
$(g,f)$ for $i=0,1$, to $(g,g)$ for $i=2$, to $(f,g)$ for $i=3$,
and to $(f,f)$ for $i=4$. The comma category $x\downarrow u$ has
five $S$-vertices $(S_i,h)$ and ten $T$-vertices
$(T_i,c),(T_i,d)$, and twenty nonidentity arrows. It is connected.
Its nerve is a graph, with $H_1\cong\mathbb Z^{20-15+1}
=\mathbb Z^6$; each $S$-vertex has valence four. Thus its component
is neither isomorphic nor homotopy equivalent to a circle, although
$fc=gc$ and its noncontractibility is exactly as asserted in the
corrected proposition. The complete composition table, all typed
composable triples, and these graph counts are checked by
\texttt{akr\_nonmonic\_comma\_circle.py} and its supplied output.
notes: Three objects, eight arrows; comma graph H1=Z^6. Stable label: C:nonmonic-circle-counterexample

statement:
There exists a small nonempty connected quasi-filtered category $A$
and a covariant functor $Q:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ such that every $Q(X)$ is
finitely generated free abelian, every $Q(g)$ is split injective with
free abelian cokernel, and nevertheless
\[
 T_1(Q)\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad T_i(Q)=0\quad(i\geq2).
\]
One may take any repaired AKR category $A=K^*$ and
\[
 Q=\operatorname{coker}\bigl(D:P_W\longrightarrow P_V^2\bigr),
 \qquad D(t)=\bigl(t(v_2-v_1),t(v_3-v_1)\bigr).
\]
Thus pointwise freeness and split injectivity do not by themselves
close the cycle-module colimit obstruction.
notes: Quasi-filtered AKR, finite free values, split injections, T1=Z; totality not asserted. Stable label: C:split-monic-counterexample

statement:
For the same quasi-filtered category $A=K^*$ there is a covariant
functor $\Gamma:A\to\mathrm{Grp}$ such that every $\Gamma(X)$ is a
finitely generated free group and every transition map identifies its
source with a free factor of its target, but the abelianization
functor $\Gamma_{\rm ab}:A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ has
$T_1(\Gamma_{\rm ab})\cong\mathbb Z$.
notes: Proved: the same obstruction with free groups and free-factor maps Stable label: C:free-group-counterexample

statement:
There is a diagram of finitely generated free groups, with every
transition a free-factor inclusion and with free group colimit, whose
ordinary simplicial-set colimit of nerves has second integral homology
$\mathbb Z$.
notes: Finite parallel-pair index, not quasi-filtered. Free values and free-factor transitions do not make the ordinary nerve colimit aspherical. Stable label: C:freefactor-nerve

statement:
Let $A$ be a finite stage, or a full finite substage containing $V,W$
and every prescribed incoming generator and factorization for its
retained targets, of the repaired AKR construction. Adjoin a
single quasi-filter target $Z$ for $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ and write
$A'$ for the resulting category. Put $s=4k+1$, where $k\geq n$, and
write $\alpha_i:T\to Z$, $i\in\mathbb Z/s$, for its generating maps.
All old objects and arrows remain unchanged. For an object $X$ let
$G_X$ have vertices $A(V,X)$ and one directed edge $b$ from $bv_1$ to
$bv_2$ for each $b\in A(W,X)$, using $A'$ when $X=Z$. Let
$K(X)=H_1(G_X;\mathbb Z)$ and $Q=\operatorname{colim}_A K$.

Let $F\subseteq G_S$ be the equalizer subgraph: its vertices are those
$c:V\to S$ with $fc=gc$, and its edges are those $b:W\to S$ with
$fb=gb$. Then
\[
 \ker\bigl(Q\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{A'}K\bigr)
 =\left\langle [(g_\#-f_\#)\sigma]\ :\
 \sigma\in C_1(G_S;\mathbb Z),\quad
 \partial\sigma=w-v,\quad v,w\in F_0\right\rangle.
 \tag{FP}
\]
Only pairs $v,w$ lying in the same component of $G_S$ occur. A path may
be chosen for $\sigma$; reversing edges is represented by negative
coefficients. The displayed difference is a cycle in $G_T$, and its
class in $Q$ is independent of the chosen path. It is enough to choose
one vertex from each component of $F$ and paths joining those
representatives which lie in a common component of $G_S$.

Consequently this attachment preserves $Q$, and hence the old second
homology of the binary category of elements, if
\[
 \pi_0(F)\longrightarrow\pi_0(G_S)
 \quad\hbox{is injective}.
 \tag{FC}
\]
More generally, preservation holds if and only if all classes in
\eqref{eq:akr-fixed-path-kernel} are zero in $Q$; injectivity in
\eqref{eq:akr-fixed-components} is sufficient but is not asserted to be
necessary.
notes: Every repaired attachment with prescribed covered target. Exact kernel formula; no all-stage vanishing inferred. Stable label: C:fixed-path-kernel

statement:
Consider a repaired attachment for injections $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$
between finite sets. Assume that the partial relation
$f(x)\mapsto g(x)$ has no nontrivial directed cycles.
Let $F=\{f(x):f(x)=g(x)\}$ and write the nonconstant directed paths of
the partial relation $f(x)\mapsto g(x)$ as
\[
 p_{\nu,0}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow p_{\nu,l_\nu-1}.
\]
Here $l_\nu$ is the number of vertices of the path, not its number of
edges. Put $L=\max_\nu l_\nu$, or $L=1$ when there are no such paths.
For $s=4k+1$ and $k\geq n\geq L$, let
$\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{4k}:T\to Z$ be the repaired copy maps.
For $0\leq i<j\leq4k$, their set of fixed source vertices is exactly:
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $(i,j)=(r,4k-r)$ with $0\leq r\leq L-2$, it is
\[
 F\ \cup\ \{p_{\nu,t}:0\leq t\leq l_\nu-r-2\};
\]
\item if $(i,j)=(2k-r,2k+1+r)$ with $0\leq r\leq L-2$, it is
\[
 F\ \cup\ \{p_{\nu,t}:r+1\leq t\leq l_\nu-1\};
\]
\item for all other pairs it is $F$.
\end{enumerate}
An empty index range contributes no points. Thus at most $2L-1$
distinct fixed subsets have to be tested, independently of $s$.
notes: Exact prefix/suffix classification for every actual point path size and k at least the common bound; at most 2L-1 subsets. Stable label: C:beta-fixed-subsets

statement:
Assume that $f$ and $g$ induce injections on binary graph components
and that their underlying point images meet in at most one point.
Then every equalizer subgraph of a pair of copy maps
$\alpha_i,\alpha_j:T\to Z$ is connected in each component of $G_T$.
Thus the fixed-path criterion applies to a subsequent attachment for
any such copy pair, even when $K(T)/F(T)$ is nonzero.
notes: Component injections and point-image overlap at most one imply the stated next-copy fixed-set criterion. Stable label: C:beta-small-overlap

statement:
In any repaired AKR Construction C.1, let $P_+$ and $P_-$ be the fresh
first-stage quasi-filter targets for $(v_1,v_2)$ and $(v_2,v_1)$.
Write $s_+,s_-$ for their respective numbers of quasi-filter maps.
In the binary graph $G_{P_\pm}$, let $S_\pm$ be the $s_\pm$ vertices
of its unique circular component, and choose its integral cycle
$\kappa_\pm$ with augmentation one. For $X\in K^*$ define
\[
 F(X)=\mathbb Z[K^*(P_+,X)]\oplus\mathbb Z[K^*(P_-,X)],
 \qquad
 \iota_X(b)=b\kappa_\pm\in K(X)
 \quad(b:P_\pm\to X).
\]
Then $\iota:F\to K$ is a natural monomorphism. Its quotient $M=K/F$
is pointwise a finitely generated free abelian group, and every arrow
of $K^*$ induces a split injection on $M$ with free abelian cokernel.
The splitting is an existence statement for each individual arrow;
no compatible family of splittings is asserted.

More precisely, if $X\in K_m$, $m\geq1$, $g:Y\to X$ is any arrow,
and $h_i:P_{\epsilon_i}\to X$ is a finite family of distinct typed
arrows, then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|h_i(S_{\epsilon_i})\cap g(Y)|\geq3$ implies that $h_i$
factors through $g$;
\item if every displayed intersection has at most two points, then
\[
 \left|\bigcup_i h_i(S_{\epsilon_i})\setminus g(Y)\right|
 \geq\frac{a_m}{a_1}\sum_i(s_{\epsilon_i}-2).
\]
\end{enumerate}
These assertions hold for mixed families with either source $P_+$ or
$P_-$.
notes: All-stage pointwise and relative result; not injectivity after taking colimit. Stable label: C:protected-cycles

statement:
Use the protected objects $P_+,P_-$, their marked circles $S_+,S_-$,
and their cycle generators from Theorem~\ref{C:protected-cycles}.
For every object $X$ of the repaired construction, every protected
arrow $h:P_\epsilon\to X$, and every arrow $g:Y\to X$, the following
stronger routing assertion holds. If $h(S_\epsilon)\cap g(Y)$ contains
the images of two vertices which are not adjacent in $S_\epsilon$,
then $h$ factors through $g$. Consequently, if $h$ does not factor
through $g$, that intersection is empty, a single vertex, or two
adjacent vertices. The boundary graphs of two distinct protected cells
in $G_X$ meet in an empty set, one vertex, or one edge.
notes: All admissible stages: a proper protected-circle overlap is empty, a vertex, or one edge. Stable label: C:protected-nonadjacent

statement:
Let $P(X)\subseteq K(X)\subseteq C_1(G_X;\mathbb Z)$ be the subgroup
freely generated by the protected cycles in
Theorem~\ref{C:protected-cycles}. For any two arrows
$f:Y\to X$ and $g:Z\to X$, let $U\subseteq G_X$ be the union of
their image subgraphs. Then
\[
 P(X)\cap C_1(U;\mathbb Z)
 = f_\#P(Y)+g_\#P(Z).
 \tag{PI}
\]
The same assertion holds with coefficients in an arbitrary abelian
group. Thus a protected-cycle combination whose edge support lies in
the union uses only protected cells factoring through one of those
two arrows.
notes: Objectwise two-image saturation over every abelian coefficient group; no colimit saturation inferred. Stable label: C:protected-two-images

statement:
Let $S,T$ be finite simple graphs and let $f,g:S\to T$ be induced
graph embeddings. Suppose each connected component of each image
is geodesically convex in $T$, and that both embeddings induce
injections on connected components. Suppose also that the directed
graph with edges $f(x)\to g(x)$ whenever $f(x)\ne g(x)$ has no
directed cycle. Then the induced subgraph on
\[
 F=\{x\in S:f(x)=g(x)\}
\]
is geodesically convex within each connected component of $S$.
In particular its intersection with every component of $S$ is
empty or connected.
notes: Proved: fixed sets of convex partial isometries Stable label: C:convex-fixed

statement:
The repaired quasi-filter construction supplies the no-cycle
hypothesis for its defining parallel pair. The lemma therefore
reduces connectedness of its fixed-point intersections to convexity
and component injectivity of the old arrows. Neither convexity
preservation under every admissible quasi-filter attachment nor
the resulting universal-choice persistence is proved here.
Proposition~\ref{C:fixed-path-kernel} supplies the exact cycle-space
comparison, and Theorem~\ref{C:selected-nontotal} completes the
induction for a controlled choice of large targets. The remaining
universal assertion must not be inferred from those choices or from
the finite verifications below.
notes: Open in this incomplete record: convexity induction Stable label: C:convex-obligation

statement:
For arbitrary finite graphs, convex image components, injectivity on
connected components, and bounded point-transition paths do not suffice
to ensure that the repaired beta gluing is injective on connected
components of each old copy. This assertion concerns a generic graph
construction; the displayed arrow configuration is not asserted to
occur in the category generated by C.1.
notes: Generic repaired graph gluing only; not shown to occur in C.1. Stable label: C:generic-component-warning

statement:
For a generic pair of induced graph embeddings with connected source
and target, strong convexity of both source images, injectivity on
components, and bounded nontrivial point paths do not guarantee
convexity of the old copies in the repaired beta target. This failure
can occur at $n=3$, $s=45$, $k=11$, even though these numbers satisfy
the numerical C.1 condition for $a_0=2$, $a_1=8/5$.
The graph configuration below is not asserted to arise among the
arrows of the prescribed C.1 construction.
notes: Connected source and target, all old images strongly convex, point paths of size two, and numerically admissible s=45. A 46-edge path shortens to 45; no realization as actual C.1 arrows is claimed. Stable label: C:connected-convex-warning

statement:
Let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be injections of finite sets. Suppose
the nonidentity part of the relation $f(x)\mapsto g(x)$ has only directed
paths. Let $n\geq2$ bound their numbers of vertices, choose $k\geq n$,
and put $s=4k+1$. Let
\[
 \alpha_i:T\longrightarrow Z_k,\qquad i\in\mathbb Z/s,
\]
be the actual-path-length repaired beta maps. Define
\[
 (\lambda_i,\mu_i)=
 \begin{cases}
 (g,f),&0\leq i<2k,\\
 (g,g),&i=2k,\\
 (f,g),&2k<i<4k,\\
 (f,f),&i=4k.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then $Z_k$ is the coequalizer in sets of
\[
 \coprod_{i\in\mathbb Z/s}S
 \rightrightarrows
 \coprod_{i\in\mathbb Z/s}T,
 \qquad
 (i,x)\longmapsto(i,\lambda_i x),\quad
 (i,x)\longmapsto(i+1,\mu_i x).
 \tag{NC}
\]
In particular, compatible maps from the displayed copies of $T$ to
any set induce a unique map from $Z_k$.
notes: Proved: the repaired target is the strict necklace colimit Stable label: C:necklace-set-colimit

statement:
Let $S,T$ be finite linearly ordered sets and let
$f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be increasing injections. Fix $n\geq2$
at least the number of vertices in every nontrivial path of the relation
$f(x)\mapsto g(x)$. There is an integer $K\geq n$ such that, for every
$k\geq K$, the covered repaired target $Z_k$ admits a linear order
making every generating map $\alpha_i:T\to Z_k$ increasing.
The prescribed order on $T$ is unchanged. The assertion permits any
additional lower bounds on $k$.
notes: All sufficiently large k, with a terminating finite choice procedure; no assertion at every smaller admissible k. Stable label: C:ordered-necklace

statement:
The proposition asserts existence for all sufficiently large $k$;
it does not assert orderability at every minimally admissible value.
Its proof is a strict set-colimit argument and uses no conversion
of a homotopy-coherent cocone into a strict one.

The choice can be made effectively. Place $T$ at integer coordinates
and choose the piecewise-linear $h$ just described, with rational
coefficients. Its fixed intervals and the endpoints of the other
components are determined by finitely many affine equations. Iterate
the finitely many rational points $g(x)$ and increase $k$ until
\eqref{eq:akr-order-separation} holds, together with all additional
numerical lower bounds. The convergence argument proves termination.
The subsequent prescriptions for $w$ and $\rho$ are finite and rational.
Thus arbitrary tie-breaking in the last step may also be replaced by
a fixed deterministic ordering rule.
notes: Proved scope and effective parameter selection Stable label: C:ordered-necklace-scope

statement:
Let $f,g:S\rightrightarrows T$ be a parallel pair at a finite stage of
the repaired AKR construction. Suppose that each of the induced graph
embeddings $G_S\to G_T$ is injective on connected components and that
the image of each component is geodesically convex. Here geodesically
convex means that every shortest graph path between two of its
vertices lies in that image. Let $D$ be the largest diameter of a
component of the finite graph $G_T$, taking the diameter of a singleton
to be zero. Choose the repaired path bound $n\geq2$ and a parameter
$s=4k+1$, $k\geq n$, such that
\[
 s>(2n-2)(D+1).
 \tag{LC}
\]
Then every generating map $\alpha_i:T\to Z$ of the repaired target
has geodesically convex image on each component of $G_T$.
This lemma alone does not assert injectivity on components of
$G_T\to G_Z$.
notes: Strong geodesic convexity follows from the explicit strict diameter/visibility bound; component injection is proved separately. Stable label: C:large-target-convexity

statement:
For every sequence $(a_m)$ satisfying the numerical requirements of
the repaired AKR Construction C.1, one can choose its finite targets
so that all of the following hold at every stage:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the underlying point sets $X$, and separately the sets
 $H(X)=\pi_0G_X$, admit linear orders for which every arrow
 induces an increasing injection on each of these two sets;
\item every arrow image component in $G_X$ is geodesically convex;
\item every attachment induces an injection on the second integral
 homology of the binary category of elements.
\end{enumerate}
For the resulting countable union $A=\bigcup_mK_m$, the action
\[
 H=h_V/(bv_1\sim bv_2)
\]
satisfies
\[
 H_2(B\operatorname{El}_A H;\mathbb Z)\ne0.
\]
In particular there exists a quasi-filtered category which is not
total. This is an existence theorem about selected sufficiently
large targets; it does not assert the universal choice statement
of Part C.1.
depends_on: C.5 [C:attachment-cycle-test]; C.16 [C:convex-fixed]; C.10 [C:fixed-path-kernel]; C.23 [C:large-target-convexity]; C.20 [C:necklace-set-colimit]; C.21 [C:ordered-necklace]
notes: Every admissible a-sequence admits selected large targets with persistent binary H2. A deterministic countable example is specified. Decides total strictly contained in quasi-filtered, not universal C.1 or A.1. Stable label: C:selected-nontotal

statement:
Let $C$ be a small category and let $n\geq1$. Every free homotopy class of
maps $S^n\to |NC|$ has a representative $|Nv|:|ND|\to |NC|$, after a
homeomorphism $|ND|\cong S^n$, where $D$ is the poset of nonempty faces of
a finite triangulation of $S^n$ and $v:D\to C$ is a functor.
notes: Known, with the reduction proved: finite-poset representatives Stable label: FT:sphere-representatives

statement:
Let $A$ be a small nonempty connected category. For a functor
$u:D\to A$, define the covariant $A$-set
\[
 H_u(a)=\pi_0(u\downarrow a),\qquad
 H_u(b)([d,f])=[d,bf]
\]
for $b:a\to a'$. Here $(d,f)$ has $f:u(d)\to a$, and an arrow
$(d,f)\to(d',f')$ is $\delta:d\to d'$ with $f'u(\delta)=f$.
Define a functor
\[
 j_u:D\longrightarrow\operatorname{El}_A(H_u),\qquad
 d\longmapsto(u(d),[d,1_{u(d)}]),
\]
whose value on an arrow is its image under $u$. The following conditions
are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every component of every $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$, for every
covariant $H:A\to\mathsf{Set}$, is weakly contractible.
\item For every finite poset $D$ and every $u:D\to A$, $Bj_u$ is
null-homotopic on every connected component of $BD$.
\item The same conclusion holds when $D$ is the face poset of a finite
triangulation of $S^n$, for every integer $n\geq1$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular the tests in (3) suffice; no bound on the dimension of the
spheres is being imposed.
notes: Proved: Lead 6 Stable label: FT:finite-test

statement:
Let $\mathsf{Ty}$ be the category in PRETOT Definition E.1: its objects
are finite words $\tau$ in $+,-$, including the empty word, and a morphism
$\tau\to\rho$ is an endpoint-preserving functor
$I_\tau\to I_\rho$ whose function on vertices is nondecreasing. Here
$I_\tau$ is the free category on the oriented line prescribed by $\tau$.
Then $\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is isomorphic to the category of these
words and nondecreasing sign-preserving maps of their letter sets.

Put $p=(++)$, $q=(+-+)$, and use one-based letter indices. The arrows
\[
 e=(1,3),\quad c=(1,1):p\rightrightarrows q
\]
have no completion to a commutative square. For every nonzero unital
commutative ring $R$ they have no affine equalizer in
$\operatorname{Aff}_R(\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}})$.
In fact, for the covariant set quotient
\[
 H=\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}(p,-)/(ge\sim gc)
\]
we have
$H_1(B\operatorname{El}_{\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}}(H);\mathbb Z)
\cong\mathbb Z$. Thus $\mathsf{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is neither total nor
exact. The phrase ``over any ring'' in Lead 8 must exclude the zero ring;
with that qualification the lead is true.
notes: Nonzero commutative rings only; zero ring refutes literal any-ring wording. Stable label: FT:ty

statement:
Suppose $A$ is a small total category that is not exact, and let
$a_0,\ldots,a_k:p\to q$ be a family without an integral affine equalizer.
Assume $k$ is least among all such families in $A$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A(q,p)=\varnothing$.
\item The finite cardinalities $|A(p,x)|$ have no uniform finite bound;
in symbols, $\sup_x|A(p,x)|=\infty$ in the sense of unboundedness in the
natural numbers, allowing infinite values.
\item The full cosieve
$V_p=\{x\in A:A(p,x)\ne\varnothing\}$ is again a separator, with the
same exhibited family. Its object $p$ is weakly initial, and the minimal
integer $k$ remains the same after restriction.
\item For every arrow $g:q\to x$, the arrows
$ga_0,\ldots,ga_k:p\to x$ are pairwise distinct.
\end{enumerate}
notes: Proved: Lead 9 Stable label: FT:minimal-family

statement:
Among nonempty connected small categories,
\[
 \{\text{filtered}\}\subsetneq\{\text{exact}\}
 \subseteq\{\text{total}\}\subsetneq\{\text{quasi-filtered}\}.
\]
The ordinal-injection category witnesses the first strict inclusion.
The selected repaired AKR category of
Theorem~\ref{C:selected-nontotal} witnesses the last strict inclusion.
Whether the middle inclusion is an equality remains undecided here.
depends_on: B.2 [B:row-audit]; C.4 [C:akr-all-rings]; C.24 [C:selected-nontotal]; Source: AdamekKoubekReiterman1981; Source: Isbell1974; Source: IsbellMitchell1973; Source: IsbellMitchell1976
manuscript_pages_settled: II ms. 36-36ter; strict first and last inclusions, middle comparison unresolved
notes: Proved: the class diagram with strict right inclusion Stable label: D:known-diagram

statement:
We have not decided whether exactness equals totality. The other
comparison is now decided: totality is strictly stronger than
quasi-filteredness, by Theorem~\ref{C:selected-nontotal}. The selected
AKR category is not total and therefore is not a separator for the
remaining middle inclusion.
notes: Only exact versus total remains unresolved; total is strictly contained in quasi-filtered. Stable label: D:undecided-inclusions

statement:
The implication \emph{totalement $W_\infty$-asph\'erique
$\Longrightarrow$ filtrante} at II manuscript page 36ter is false.
For nonempty connected small $A$,
\[
 A\text{ filtered}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 A\text{ total and sifted}.
\]
For every fixed integer $n\geq1$,
\[
\begin{split}
 A\text{ filtered}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad&
 A\text{ total and }
 \hocolim_A K(M(a),n)\text{ is }n\text{-truncated}\\
 &\text{for every covariant }M:A\to\Ab.
\end{split}
\]
The implication from siftedness alone to totality in Proposition
2.19 at II manuscript page 36 is false.
manuscript_pages_settled: II ms. 36-36ter; XII ms. 88-89 (stated corrected implications)
notes: Refuted conjecture; known corrected implications Stable label: D:manuscript

statement:
For every small category $A$, including empty and disconnected
categories, let $\ell:A\to\Pi A$ be groupoid completion. For
every fixed finite $n\geq1$, homotopy colimits over $A$ preserve
$n$-types if and only if
\[
 C_a=a\downarrow\ell
 =\El_A\bigl(\Hom_{\Pi A}(a,\ell(-))\bigr)
\]
is filtered for every $a$. This is supplied TOTEX D.10.
notes: Known, with the comparison maps audited: positive truncations Stable label: D:truncation

statement:
At II manuscript page 36, for $f:X\to Y$, finality must use
$y\backslash X$ rather than the printed $y\backslash Y$.
The latter always has initial object $\id_y$ and would make
the condition vacuous. At XII manuscript page 88,
$H'\in(U')^\wedge$, so the correctly typed isomorphism is
\[
 U'/t'\simeq U'/H',
\]
not $U'/t'\simeq U/H'$. A presheaf on $U$ is a covariant
set-valued functor on $U^{\mathrm{op}}$; its usual element
category is opposite to the corresponding covariant element
category. Opposition preserves the classifying-space homotopy type.

Definition 1 at XII manuscript pages 88--89 quantifies over
all left Kan extensions and equivalently over ordinary final
images. It is the notion used here, distinct from the
test-category diagonal condition in \emph{Pursuing Stacks}.
We inspected the supplied transcription, not an independent
copy of the authoritative edition. These are mathematical
typing corrections, not a new editorial collation.
